definition: The production of a computer model of a process or system, used to study or predict its behaviour under different conditions.
origin: From Latin simulare (to imitate, copy), from similis (like). Computer-based simulation developed as a scientific method in the mid-20th century, notably to model nuclear reactions and weather.
